description: Portable identity log. A verifier MUST accept every log under "accept" under the stated attestation policy and derive exactly the expected values, and MUST refuse every log under "reject". A relying party holding the pin under "admission" (and, where "pinned" is not null, the log it holds for that pin, which ends at the pinned head, and the rehome refusals under "refusals" that it holds for the identity) MUST reach exactly the expected judgement, and MUST answer each "push" message with exactly the expected acknowledgment under the same convention. A verifier MUST accept every refusal under "refusals.accept", refuse every one under "refusals.reject", and reach the expected comparison under "refusals.contradictions". Refusal reasons of the verifier are not normative; admission reasons are. All keys here are published test keys.

accept.why: rotation, recovery and a recovery-policy change, every head attested; heads 1 and 3 took effect at the lease barrier, after acceptance
the same history with no attestations, for a verifier that accepts unattested heads
the same history with its FINAL instant moved one millisecond and no attestation: the log alone cannot detect this, the head digest differs, and only an attestation or a pinned checkpoint exposes it
a move to a second resolver, signed by the recovery quorum alone, then a recovery there; heads before the move are attested by the first resolver, the move and what follows by the second
the same move with no attestations
a resolver key rotation: a move to the same resolver id under a new key
the format 1 encoding of a history without moves

reject.why: unattested heads where the verifier requires attestation
entries reordered
a middle entry dropped
the genesis entry dropped
an entry repeated
an INTERIOR instant moved one millisecond: the next transition's owner-signed expected_digest no longer matches
the genesis instant moved one millisecond
the final instant moved while its attestation still describes the original head
an instant before the transition's signed window
an instant beyond expires_at - 1 + lease + margin
a genesis instant outside the enrollment window
a transition signature replaced by another valid signature
a transition body altered after signing
the new key's possession signature removed
a head attested by a key the owner never enrolled
an attestation moved to a different entry
an attestation naming a different resolver epoch
a rotation signed only by the recovery quorum
a recovery signed only by the operational quorum
a rotation that changes recovery authority
a retired operational key reinstated
a retired recovery key reinstated
the resolver key given control of the person
a skipped sequence number
a transition naming a predecessor that is not the previous head
a signed window longer than 300,000 ms
an unknown format
an extra top-level member
an extra entry member
a transition on the genesis entry
no entries
a move signed by the operational quorum
a move signed by a retired recovery key
a move whose epoch does not advance
a move whose epoch skips
a move that does not leave the current resolver
a move from a head that is not the current head
a move naming a current control key as the resolver key
a move naming a retired control key as the resolver key
a move whose audience is not an exact origin
a move taking effect before its signed window
a move taking effect at the end of its signed window: a move has no lease barrier to reproduce
the move attested by the first resolver, which it leaves
a head after the move attested by the first resolver
an entry carrying both a transition and a move
a format 1 log carrying a move
after a move, a rotation signed with keys retired before it

precedence.why: the owner moved to a second resolver; a thief with the old operational key forked at the first resolver: the higher epoch supersedes wherever the fork is
the same pair the other way round
two forks at one epoch: a conflict, never resolved by choosing
a branch forked by a recovery key the other history retired (recovery-policy at head 3), at a higher epoch than the owner's move: a conflict, never superseded
the same retired-key branch against the owner's history that never moved: a conflict
one history is a prefix of the other

admission.why: a pin at head 0 admits the attested history: advanced
the same pin admits the move, whose heads are attested by the resolver of each epoch: advanced
a pin already at the log's head: unchanged
a move whose rehome entry no resolver attested is not admitted under ANY attestation policy: the owner consented, but no destination adopted (unadopted-move)
a pin that already followed the move, shown the same log again: unchanged
a pin that verified a resolution at head 4, shown a history that stops at head 3: behind, which is not evidence either way
a pin whose checkpoint sits on a rival branch at the same epoch: conflict, never resolved by choosing

the same rival checkpoint against the owner's move, the party holding the rival history it pinned: the recovery quorum the move forked under is still current there, so the higher epoch supersedes, and the superseded checkpoint is reported
the same, but the party holds only the pin: it cannot rule out a retired recovery authority, so conflict (fail closed)
a pin enrolled with a resolver key the log never names: foreign-lineage
a pin at epoch 1 shown a history that never left epoch 0: foreign-lineage
a pin for another identity: another-identity
a log that fails verification: invalid-log
unattested heads under a strict policy: invalid-log
a pin taken after the recovery-policy, shown a higher-epoch fork signed by the recovery key it retired, holding the pinned history: conflict, never superseded
the same with only the pin: conflict
a pin that followed the owner's move, shown the retired-key fork, holding the pinned history: conflict
a pin taken BEFORE the recovery-policy, shown the retired-key fork first: advanced; nothing it holds shows the retirement yet
that party, now holding the fork it admitted, is shown the owner's real history: conflict, so it learns of the retirement instead of staying silently on the fork
a party holding the destination's refusal of the rehome, shown the log in which that destination nevertheless attested the head the rehome produced: refused-move
the same refusal against the dangling consent nobody attested: refused-move, which a held refusal decides before the evidence rule
a held refusal of a different rehome says nothing about this one: advanced
a held "refusal" the named destination did not sign is no refusal: advanced

a party already past the refused move (it admitted it before the destination refused), shown the log again with no later move: refused-move; the refusal arrived late, and nothing in the log escapes it
the same party shown the owner's escape rehome: the recovery quorum moves the identity from the refusing destination to a third resolver, which adopts it: advanced
the same party shown an "escape" back to the refusing destination at the next epoch: refused-move, rehoming back to it does not count
the same party shown an "escape" to the refusing destination's resolver id under a new key: refused-move, it is the same destination
the same party shown the escape rehome that the third resolver never attested: unadopted-move, the escape needs the next destination's adoption like every move
a party still at the first resolver, holding the refusal, shown the escaped log: advanced; the refusal is escaped for every party, and adoption evidence is still required for both moves

push.why: a relying party that enrolled the identity at the first resolver admits the pushed move
the same push again, against the pin the first one produced: unchanged, so a wallet may repeat it freely
a relying party that never enrolled the identity: unknown-identity
a message whose log does not verify: invalid-log, and no identity is named
a message in an unknown format: invalid-log
a history that stops before the party checkpoint: behind
anyone pushes the retired-key fork to a party that pinned after the recovery-policy and holds that history: conflict
the same push to a party holding only the pin: conflict
the owner pushes the real history to a party that admitted the fork and holds it: conflict
a push of a move whose rehome the party holds a refusal for: refused-move
the same push to a party holding a refusal the named destination did not sign: advanced
the owner pushes the escape rehome to a party stranded past the refused move, which holds only its pin: advanced

accept.why: the destination the rehome names refuses it

reject.why: a refusal signed by the former resolver, which the rehome does not name
a refusal signed by a stranger
a refusal naming another rehome digest
a refusal naming another epoch
a refusal of a different rehome presented against this one
a refusal body altered after signing
a refusal with an extra member
a refusal with two signatures

contradictions.why: the refused rehome produced a head the destination attested: the destination equivocated, and the pair proves it
the refused rehome sits in a log but no one attested its head: a dangling consent, consistent with the refusal
a log that never contains the refused rehome
a log whose move is a different rehome from the same head
